Title: Card idea: Delayed Gratification (Sabbat Political Action)

Messages.Author: LunaSlave
Messages.Body:
I've been trying to think of ideas that alter what happens when a Methuselah gets ousted...which made me think of my previous card idea, Diminishing Returns. I've also been thinking about ways to make Sabbat politics more powerful, but different from Parity Shift. I'm not great at templating, but I like this idea...

Here, my friends, is the result.

Delayed Gratification
Political Action
Requires an Archbishop, Cardinal or Regent
Choose a Methuselah. The next time the chosen Methuselah's prey is ousted, he or she is not rewarded with pool immediately. Instead, the pool is gained during the chosen Methuselah's next untap phase afterwards.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
I can't think of any deck I'd like to put this card in. The effect seems too minor and random to be worth (I'll have only 1 turn to try to kill him before he gets his pool, but I can't really control when he will oust his prey).

What do you think about:

Name: Delayed Gratification
Cardtype: Political Action
Requires an Archbishop, Cardinal or Regent
Choose another Methuselah who is not chosen by a Delayed Gratification. If this referendum is successful, put this card in play. The next time the chosen Methuselah's prey is ousted, the pool he or she should earn goes on this card instead of his or her pool. During his or her untap phase, he or she moves a counter to his or her pool.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Unless I missed something, I prefer to put the card in play because:
- it's easier to remember than a token ("is that a pool?" one may ask after a few turns)
- the card text is always visible
- it's easier to keep track of the pool yet to gain to put it on the card

Messages.Author: LunaSlave
Messages.Body: I agree with Ankha, putting it on the card is much more elegant. The only change I'd make to the first version is allowing Prisci to call it, something I basically left out of the original, too weak card just by simply forgetting to include them. Of course it would require playtesting, but I think a card like that would actually be printable, uniquely interesting, and fairly rewarding to Sabbat politics. The situational negotiations that could go on when placing this card on a Methuselah other than your prey are very interesting, too.
